risk_if_not_implemented: Without Control Applicability Boundary Graphical Representation, adversaries may move laterally, exfiltrate data or reach systems that should have been isolated from untrusted networks. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Network Security Controls (NSC)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, govern & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of Network Security Controls (NSC).
compensating_control_1.justification: Network Security Controls (NSC) (NET-02) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Control Applicability Boundary Graphical Representation (AST-17.1) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Network Diagrams & Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to maintain network architecture diagrams that: 
(1) Contain sufficient detail to assess the security of the network's architecture;
(2) Reflect the current architecture of the network environment; and
(3) Document all sensitive and/or regulated data flows.
compensating_control_2.justification: Network Diagrams & Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs) (AST-17) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Control Applicability Boundary Graphical Representation (AST-17.1) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
